subject: Order Form: uptime thresholds, maintenance carveouts & support handoff
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acadiahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acadia Procurement <procurement@acadiahealth.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial redlines — Order Form (support + uptime)

Hi Olga / Laura,

Attached is Acadia's first pass redline of the Order Form (see acacia_orderform_redline_v1.pdf). We've focused on the SLA/support section first because our procurement/security teams need clarity on recovery expectations before we move forward. High-level asks in this pass: 

- Clarify uptime measurement windows (we need regional granularity, not a global aggregate).
- Add explicit definition of what constitutes a P1 vs P2 outage for SLA triggers.
- Limit service credit to avoid cascading credits; propose a cap at 6 months of fees.
- Define maintenance notice windows and carveouts (we prefer 30 days for planned maintenance, 48 hours for emergency/critical fixes).
- Confirm response times for P1/P2 and the escalation ladder (we need an on-call handoff process for cutovers).

We're planning an internal procurement review on Jan 12; can you confirm Redwood's stance on regional uptime tiers and if you can accept the credit cap language?

Also please confirm whether Redwood can provide a one-week dedicated support window during our planned migration cutover (tentative date in March).

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acadia Health

Attachment: acacia_orderform_redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 254KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-10T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — Order Form (support + uptime)

Thanks Maria — and thanks for the clear first pass. I pulled out the primary items and attached a short redline (OF_v3_olga_redlines.pdf) with line-level comments so Legal/Product can see edits inline. Quick summary of our read and proposed approach: 

1) Regional uptime measurement: we can expose region-specific SLOs (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU) as long as the Order Form lists explicit endpoints/regions. Aggregate reporting will remain available for billing/roll-up.

2) P1/P2 definitions: agree that we should tighten definitions. Laura / Jonas, can Legal provide a concise, non-technical definition set we can drop into the Order Form?

3) Credit cap: Redwood prefers a credits cap tied to monthly recurring fees rather than an absolute 6-month cap. Proposal: cap at 3x monthly recurring charges (MRR) per calendar year per account, with a maximum of 6 months' total credits if there's a repeated systemic failure. This gives both sides some protection.

4) Maintenance & carveouts: We can accept a 30-day notice for planned maintenance and 48-hour notice for non-critical patching. For emergency/force majeure security patches, we need to retain right to perform critical maintenance with as little as 4 hours notice — but we will provide a post-event report and scope of change.

5) Cutover dedicated support: Redwood can offer a paid, dedicated cutover support package (named engineers + priority queue) for the migration week; we'll attach pricing in the support matrix (support-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps: Jonas, Markus, can you review the attached OF_v3_olga_redlines.pdf and produce legal-friendly wording for the uptime definitions + credit staircase? Maria, if Acadia can confirm which regions/endpoints you care about most, we'll ensure the SLO table matches.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OF_v3_olga_redlines.pdf (pdf, 183KB), support-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 47KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-11T10:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: uptime thresholds, maintenance carveouts & support handoff

Olga / team — drafted suggested language below for the two core items I think Procurement will push back on. Attaching a short doc with clause text (sla_clause_suggestion.docx). Feel free to pull these directly into OF_v3.

--- suggested clause: uptime measurement & credit staircase ---
Uptime metric: "Uptime" for a given Region means the percentage of minutes in a Billing Month during which the Service's primary inference endpoints for that Region return responses to authenticated API requests without Error Rate >= 5%. Uptime will be calculated per Region, and an Aggregate Uptime will be provided for reporting only.

Credit Staircase: If Regional Uptime for a Billing Month is below 99.9% but >= 99.0%, Customer is eligible for a credit equal to 5% of that month's Regional MRR. If below 99.0% but >= 95.0%, credit equals 15% of that month's Regional MRR. If below 95.0%, credit equals 50% of that month's Regional MRR, up to a cap equal to 3x monthly Regional MRR in any rolling 12-month period.

Emergency maintenance carveout: Redwood may, in order to protect security or customer data, perform emergency maintenance with less than the standard notice period. Redwood will endeavor to provide notice as soon as practical and will publish a post-maintenance report identifying impacted Regions, duration, and customer-visible impact. Emergency maintenance where Customer traffic is unaffected by design (e.g., isolated control-plane updates) will not be eligible for credits.

I recommend we limit absolute caps to the 3x MRR ladder and avoid an unconditional 6-month fee credit — it's asymmetric and makes financial forecasting hard.

I'll iterate if Procurement pushes for different percentage ladders.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla_clause_suggestion.docx (docx, 12KB)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acadiahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acadia Procurement <procurement@acadiahealth.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T18:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: uptime thresholds, maintenance carveouts & support handoff

Olga / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested language. A few negotiation points from Procurement & Engineering after reviewing Jonas's draft: 

- Regional SLOs: Acadia cannot accept a model where only reporting is regional while reconciliation is global. We need reconciliation and credits to be calculated per Region for the regions we designate (we'll send a prioritized list).

- Staircase percentages: the ladder is reasonable, but Procurement wants the top tier to start at 99.95% for critical regions (production inference for patient-facing apps). For non-critical regions (dev/staging), 99.9% is acceptable.

- Credit cap: Procurement will accept the 3x MRR cap if Redwood agrees to an absolute maximum of 6 months' equivalent in very limited circumstances (systemic fail across multiple Regions) — if you can put that into a trigger clause with an agreed remediation plan, that may be acceptable.

- Maintenance: 30-day planned notice is OK. For security emergency patches we can accept accelerated windows, but Acadia requires a minimum of 24 hours notice for anything that could affect request latency. 4 hours is too short for our ops teams.

- Cutover support: we appreciate the paid week-of support offer. Procurement expects Redwood to include an onboarding runbook and on-call contact list as part of that package (we need names/titles and escalation steps).

We'd like to resolve these items prior to our procurement meeting on Jan 12. If Redwood can accept the per-Region reconciliation requirement and adjust the emergency notice to 24 hours, we can likely greenlight the commercial terms subject to final legal review.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acadia Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acadiahealth.com>, Acadia Procurement <procurement@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-12T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Final coordination & next steps — Order Form SLA items

Maria — good notes and thanks for the clarity. Quick summary of where we can align and outstanding asks so your procurement/legal team has a single doc to review: 

Agreed / Redwood concessions:
- Credits and reconciliation will be calculated per Region for the Regions Acadia designates (please send the prioritized list by EOD Jan 13).
- Credit staircase: we'll adopt Jonas's proposed ladder but accept a Producer exception where critical Regions can start at 99.95% for top tier; we'll flag those Regions in the Order Form.
- Cap: primary cap will be 3x monthly Regional MRR in a rolling 12-month window. We will include a narrowly defined systemic-failure clause that allows for up to 6 months' equivalent credit only if an agreed remediation plan is triggered and mutually accepted by Redwood and Acadia.
- Planned maintenance: 30 days notice. For security/emergency patches we can shorten notice, but Redwood accepts a minimum of 24 hours notice when the change may materially affect customer request latency.
- Cutover support: Redwood will provide a week-of paid cutover engagement and include an onboarding runbook + named on-call contacts. We will share the runbook and contact roster by Jan 19.

Open items / action items:
- Acadia: send the list of Regions/endpoints that must be reconciled per-Region (ACTION: Maria) — due: 2028-01-13 EOD.
- Redwood Legal (Jonas): draft the systemic-failure trigger language for the 6-month exceptional cap and place it into OF_v3 (ACTION: Jonas) — due: 2028-01-15.
- Redwood Product/Eng (Markus): confirm whether any of our control-plane or cross-region maintenance types are designed to be latency-neutral, and provide classification by Jan 17.
- Redwood Commercial (Olga/Laura): prepare a final redline set (OF_v3_olga_redlines.pdf -> final-redline-summary.pdf) and DocuSign envelope once legal agrees on the systemic-failure clause.

If Acadia is comfortable with the above, we'll route the final Order Form to DocuSign and aim to complete signatures within one week of the legal sign-off. I'll start the DocuSign prep once we incorporate Jonas's systemic clause and we confirm the Regions list.

Thanks all — we'll be ready to jump on a 30-minute sync if Procurement wants to walk through the changes live.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: final-redline-summary.pdf (pdf, 98KB)
